name: deutsch-atlas

scripts.check: astro sync && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p worker/tsconfig.json && bun run --cwd tools/astro-check check

//overrides: Security floors only. Each version already satisfies its parent's declared range (astro: sharp ^0.35.4; ajv: fast-uri ^3.0.1) — the pin just stops the resolver settling below the patched release. Drop an entry once its parents' own floors clear it; `bun audit` is the check. An entry that is ALSO a direct dependency must carry the identical spec string: npm rejects the pair with EOVERRIDE, so bump both or neither. Bun does not enforce that rule and the only npm in this pipeline is Cloudflare's deploy step, so the whole local gate stays green while every deploy dies — which is what happened on 2026-08-26, when #233 moved sharp to ^0.35.4 here and left ^0.35.0 below. `tests/package-manifest.test.ts` is now the gate.
//tauri-plugin-http: A Tauri plugin's JS package and Rust crate are released independently, and the Tauri CLI refuses to build on a major/minor split between them — `bun tauri build` dies at `Found version mismatched Tauri packages` while every web gate stays green. From 2026-09-15 this was held at ~2.5.9 because @tauri-apps/plugin-http 2.6.0 existed with no matching crate; on 2026-10-10 crates.io had tauri-plugin-http 2.8.1 (`cargo info tauri-plugin-http`), so it is a caret again and moves with `cargo update`. If a JS minor ever runs ahead of its crate again, pin it with ~ until the crate catches up.
//undeclared-deps: Declare every package the repo imports: workspaces use the isolated linker, so nothing is lent by hoisting. vite is a direct `import type { Connect }` in src/integrations/progress-writer.ts; keep its range in step with Astro's. sharp must be declared, not only floored under overrides: Astro's default image service needs it, and without the declaration `bun run build` dies in `generating optimized images` with MissingSharp — only on a platform where the copy is not hoisted (green on macOS, red on ubuntu-latest), after validate, test, check and lint have all passed.
//workspaces: The learner app is the root package and stays there: Astro requires its content collections to live under the project root, and content/ is shared with the editorial app, so it belongs at the repo root and the app has to meet it. Moving the app to apps/lernen and pointing `root` back at the repo was tried on 2026-08-14 — collections resolved, then the build failed in "Rearranging server assets" on every MDX outside the root that imports a component, and redirecting `root` produced a build with zero pages. apps/* holds the tools that are not the product; packages/* holds what both consume.
